sources.what: Book of Common Prayer (1662), Morning Prayer: the General Confession and the Absolution

sources.what: Book of Common Prayer (1662), The Order for the Visitation of the Sick: the special confession rubric and the absolution ('by his authority committed to me, I absolve thee')
sources.note: Checked: the page has the rubric and the absolution. This is the Anglican form of private confession, so it fits the side-by-side on confession better than Morning Prayer, and other journeys don't read it.

sources.note: Optional: one sentence on public penance in the early Church, for the lecture's history of confession.
No qualifying text: tell it in our own words, one short quotation at most.

art.title: Saint Jerome in the Wilderness
art.why: A penitent alone, his bare chest wounded, a stone in his fist, skull and hourglass on the table: guilt turned on oneself, as Dimmesdale scourges himself in secret. Not Hester Prynne (no NGA painting of the novel); the look must say this is Jerome, not a figure from Hawthorne. La Tour's Repentant Magdalen was wanted but is claimed by socrates.

art.title: The Good Shepherd
art.why: REUSE of an existing art id: the exact subject (the shepherd of Luke 15:4–6). The NGA has no other Good Shepherd.
No NGA painting of candlesticks as a subject or of Bishop Myriel; the bishop portraits (Francia's Averoldo, Strozzi's Grimani) are real sitters, not this story.

art.title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
art.why: REUSE, as the spec asks ('point back if used'): the father embracing the son is the picture of reconciliation. Already in art.json and bank.json.

music.why: Psalm 51 sung: the confession Dimmesdale cannot make.
'I once was lost, but now am found': Newton's hymn is Luke 15 in a slave-trader's mouth.
Written by a man who had lost his four daughters: peace that does not depend on what has been done to us.

memory.title: I acknowledged my sin
memory.source: WEB: 'I acknowledged my sin to you. / I didn’t hide my iniquity. / I said, I will confess my transgressions to Yahweh, / and you forgave the iniquity of my sin.' https://ebible.org/eng-web/PSA032.htm

memory.title: If we confess
memory.source: WEB: 'If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.' https://ebible.org/eng-web/1JN01.htm

flags: BCP 1662 Morning Prayer is also read in what-happens-at-church (Holy Communion and Morning Prayer, selected). If that journey reads the General Confession, session 3 should point back and read the Visitation of the Sick confession and absolution instead (fetched as guilt-bcp-sick). Either way it fills the side-by-side well: general confession, private absolution, Catholic confessional, Orthodox confession before an icon, Jewish teshuvah.
BCP 1662 text is under Crown letters patent in the UK only; it is public domain elsewhere and the rule (original English before 1929) is met. PLEASE CHECK the owner is content.
Session 1 painting is a Saint Jerome, not a scene from The Scarlet Letter: the look text must say so and describe only the gallery's description.
Session 5 has no painting; session 2 and 7 reuse existing art ids (tanner-shepherd, murillo-prodigal).
Pastoral: the abuse caveat (never imply victims must reconcile with abusers) belongs in sessions 4, 6 and 7, and the journey needs a pastor's review.
